sources.title: Electrek: 2027 Chevy Blazer EV drops CCS for Tesla-style NACS port
sources.notes: 2027 Blazer EV gets a NACS port instead of the CCS connector used on earlier models; GM will offer adapters for CCS.

sources.title: Electrek: Every 2027 GM EV will plug directly into Tesla Superchargers
sources.notes: Every 2027 GM EV (Blazer EV, Silverado EV, Lyriq included) has a native NACS port; plug directly into compatible Tesla Superchargers; some Supercharger sites remain Tesla-only.

sources.title: GCN: GM confirms all 12 of its 2027 model-year EVs will ship with native NACS charging ports
sources.notes: For 2026 most GM EVs keep a CCS1 port and need the GM NACS DC adapter; only the Cadillac Optiq and Chevrolet Bolt are NACS-native for 2026. All 2027 EVs, including Blazer EV, Silverado EV and Lyriq, get native NACS.

sources.title: InsideEVs: The 2027 Chevy Silverado EV gets a power bump and a NACS port
sources.notes: All 2027 Silverado EV models come from the factory with a native NACS port, which lets them use Tesla Superchargers and other NACS chargers.

sources.title: InsideEVs: Cadillac Lyriq fast charge test
sources.notes: "Cadillac states that the Lyriq has a maximum DC fast charge rate of 190 kW." (first-year Lyriq test).

sources.title: GreenCarsCompare: Cadillac Lyriq charging
sources.notes: Built on a 400 V architecture; 11.5 kW AC (19.2 kW optional) and 190 kW DC; CCS Type 1. Aggregator, no model-year split. Terms page returned 403 (not worked around); no licence or reuse statement on the pages read. Its US block shows "does not support DC fast charging" and "not sold in the USA" beside 190 kW DC, a site artefact; ignored.
